Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$. Write $\mathcal C(n)$ for the assertion that $T^j(n)=1$ for some $j\in\mathbb N$.

Let $\mathsf S$ assert that every $n>1$ has a positive $m<n$ and $r,s\in\mathbb N$ with $T^r(n)=T^s(m)$. Assume $\mathsf S$. Then

$$
\forall n>0,\ \mathcal C(n).
$$

The universal smaller-coalescence premise remains unproved; this is a conditional induction criterion.
